> # WP-D3 plan v1: netd and ipd (the network)
> 
> Worktree `./.worktrees/d3`, branch `wp-d3` at main `08848f60a`. PLAN ONLY: no code, no tracked-file edits, no commits. D3 does not touch `kernel/`, `model/` or `tests/programs/**`, and needs **no new kernel feature**. The kernel calls it uses (`send` with a transfer, `receive` with `max_transfer`, IRQ receive, `dma_alloc`, `map_device -> addr,len`, `thread_create`, `mint`, `process_*`, `map_fixed`) are all merged.
> 
> **Starting point.** SWARM lists D3 as "building / external claim unverified". No source exists: no `servers/netd` or `servers/ipd`, no network commits in any local or remote branch, and the recovery inventory says "no wp-d3 branch was among the four". This plan starts from scratch. Nothing external is merged.
> 
> ## OWNER DECISIONS (need confirmation before implementation)
> 
> Each item below is my recommendation. The ones marked [QA] also have their own spec-gap thread to the orchestrator.
> 
> 1. **smoltcp 0.14.0, pinned exactly (`=0.14.0`) with `default-features = false`.** Features: `alloc`, `medium-ethernet`, `proto-ipv4`, `socket-tcp`, and nothing else. That leaves out IPv6, DHCP, DNS, UDP, raw and ICMP sockets, IP fragmentation/reassembly, `auto-icmp-echo-reply` (no ping), `log`, `defmt`, `std` and the phy backends. Details and checks are in section 2.
> 2. **IPv4 only, static configuration, TCP only in D3.** `/net/udp` is deferred, which is a deliberate gap against NAMESPACES "/net/udp/... the same shape": milestone 1's SSH path needs none of it. The interface address and gateway come from ipd's arguments; there is no DHCP client. [QA D3-q-scope]
> 3. **Frames reach ipd as a `send` with a page transfer from netd, and ipd transmits with a `call` to netd.** This is the shape PLAN's attack suite already assumes ("ipd still receives netd's frames (sends)", answer 81). It makes D3 the first protocol that needs WIRE's anticipated **`kind` column** ("added when a protocol first needs a send"). That means an additive change to the generator `libs/wire/gen`, which W1/W2 own, and it changes WIRE's sentence "every milestone 1 typed message is a call". [QA D3-q-frames]
> 4. **Backpressure on `/net/tcp/N/data` writes.** NAMESPACES says "a waiting write remains a non-goal". Without one, a TCP sender with a full buffer can only busy-poll. The recommendation is a small additive `libs/rt` change, `FileServer::write -> Write::Wait`, parking exactly as `Read::Wait` does with the same admission and deadline. It needs a shared-runtime review round, like 157/163. The fallback, if refused, is a short Rwrite (at least 1 byte) and, when the buffer is completely full, an Rerror "busy" that the client retries after a parking ctl read that waits for "writable". [QA D3-q-write-wait]
> 5. **How the capability is represented (section 3).** Root scopes come from ipd's manifest arguments, one per root badge. Narrowing uses a typed `grant(scope)` (opcode 16 on ipd's 9P endpoint, WIRE's Granting rule); `ninep_common` `new_connection("")` gives a same-scope fresh connection, and `disconnect(id)` releases either kind. This needs a small additive `libs/rt` API so grant uses the skeleton's single `Minted` table (`NineServer::mint_rooted`). [QA D3-q-scope]
> 6. **"The box's own addresses" (section 3.4).** ipd always refuses, whatever the scope says: its own interface address(es), 127.0.0.0/8, 0.0.0.0/8, broadcast (limited and directed), 224.0.0.0/4, 240.0.0.0/4, and every `self=` prefix the manifest declares. On QEMU that is gateway 10.0.2.2/32, which reaches host loopback and so the forwarded ssh port. **Stated residual:** an address that routes back through NAT hairpinning somewhere outside the box is refused only if the manifest lists it. ipd cannot discover it. [QA D3-q-scope]
> 7. **/net file contents are typed encodings, not text.** This includes the ctl writes that WIRE already specifies, clone/ctl reads, and remote. Connect and listen completion is reported by a **parking read of ctl**, so no waiting write is needed for them. [QA D3-q-ctl]
> 8. **Evidence before R3.** A D3-owned test launcher (`tests/net`, the "rig") boots the real netd/ipd binaries through the real R2 stub, with named startup handles, on the real kernel and QEMU NIC. It is the evidence for TCP and the attack cases now. Manifest-driven boot through init stays a retained R3 / full-server gate, the same pattern as blkd's "boot integration waits". Orchestrator to confirm this is acceptable D3 acceptance evidence. [QA D3-q-bench]
> 9. **Bench: QEMU `virtio-mmio.force-legacy` defaults to on** (QEMU 10.2.2 here: "force-legacy default: on"). Both blkd and netd speak only virtio-mmio version 2, so **no real virtio driver can boot on the bench as configured**. That affects D2 as well. Fix: add `-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false` whenever a case has [disk] or [net], one line in qemu.rs. Do not add a legacy path to the drivers. [QA D3-q-bench]
> 10. **A device that lies makes netd refuse, not exit** (blkd's rule). netd resets the device (STATUS=0, which stops its DMA), then answers `failed` to every request.
> 11. **Stated residuals:**
>    - smoltcp's TCP initial sequence numbers come from one PCG32 seeded once from the kernel CSPRNG, so they are predictable after a few observations. That enables off-path injection on a hostile LAN, and one unlabelled user can observe another's connection rate. ipd picks ephemeral ports itself from `random`, so ports do not leak it.
>    - A NIC flood costs netd's weight-1000 CPU.
>    - Restart DMA hazard, Q147, same as blkd.
>    - A SYN flood can hold a listener's sockets in SYN-RECEIVED for up to its 10 s timeout.
>

> ## 1. netd: the virtio-net driver
> 
> **Crate `servers/netd`** (redoubt-netd; lib + bin netd; depends only on redoubt-rt). It mirrors blkd module for module, and IO-ARCHITECTURE's "netd inherits this decision" (our own queue, no virtio-drivers) applies. Files:
> 
> - `src/lib.rs`: the trust statement (what netd is trusted for, stated like blkd's three promises). `deny(unsafe_code)` everywhere except `kernel`.
> - `src/transport.rs`: the same `Transport` seam as blkd: reg read/write, DMA read/write, phys, len, wait_irq, now_us, fence. It is copied, not shared. Factoring a libs/virtio crate would reopen blkd's reviewed TCB, so that is a later follow-up.
> - `src/kernel.rs`: the only unsafe: volatile MMIO and DMA byte access, as blkd's four blocks. It refuses a register window shorter than CONFIG+8 (MAC plus status).
> - `src/virtio.rs`: register map (virtio 1.2 4.2.2), status handshake, net constants (5.1), DeviceError.
> - `src/rxq.rs` and `src/txq.rs`: two split virtqueues, each in **its own dma_alloc region** (below).
> - `src/device.rs`: bring-up and the two queue drivers. `src/server.rs`: the netif protocol.
> - `src/fake.rs` (host only): a hostile virtio-net device model.
> - `src/bin/netd.rs`: the two threads.
> - `tests/device.rs`, `tests/server.rs`; `fuzz/` (a cargo-fuzz crate excluded from the workspace, as servers/blkd/fuzz).
> 
> **Bring-up refuses rather than works around.**
> - The transport is version 2 only, and the device ID must be 1 (net).
> - Accept exactly VERSION_1 (32) and MAC (5); both are required, and a device without them is refused.
> - Everything else is left unaccepted: CSUM, GUEST_CSUM, all TSO/UFO, MRG_RXBUF, CTRL_VQ, STATUS, MQ, EVENT_IDX and INDIRECT_DESC. So the device may send no GSO, no merged buffers and no checksum offload.
> - FEATURES_OK must read back. MAC config is read under ConfigGeneration, retried at most 8 times.
> - QueueNumMax must be at least 16 for queue 0 (rx) and queue 1 (tx), otherwise refuse. Reset is polled a bounded number of times.
> 
> **The DMA layout. Nothing the device says is used as an index or a length.** There are two regions, each self-contained, and every address given to the device is region_phys + a constant (compile-time LAYOUT_FITS asserts, as blkd):
> 
> - **RX region** (rx thread): desc[16], avail, used, then 16 slots of 2048 B. Each slot takes the 12-byte virtio_net_hdr (v1 size) plus a frame up to 1514 B.
>   - Descriptor i always points at slot i with length 2048 and WRITE. The table and avail ring are written from constants and **never read back**.
> - **TX region** (serving thread): desc[16], avail (with NO_INTERRUPT), used, then 16 slots of 2048 B.
> 
> **What netd validates on the used ring** (read at netd's own counter, never at a device index):
> - idx advances by at most the number of outstanding buffers.
> - Each entry's id is < 16 and currently outstanding (an outstanding bitmap). A duplicate or an unknown id is a lie.
> - rx len is at least 12 and at most 2048. The header must say flags == 0 (no NEEDS_CSUM, since it was not negotiated) and gso_type == NONE.
> - The frame length is len - 12, between 14 and 1514.
> - The frame is copied out **once**, with netd's own length, before any byte is looked at.
> - tx len is ignored beyond the at-most check.
> 
> Anything else is broken (decision 10). A tx slot outstanding longer than **10 s** is also broken (blkd's timeout).
> 
> **Threads: no shared memory, no locks.** consoled's precedent is "no shared state between the two".
> - **Serving thread.** Owns the TX region and bring-up. It receives on `netd`:
>   - info and transmit from the client badge;
>   - the rx thread's one startup message, carrying the RX region's physical address in words;
>   - BROKEN from the rx thread.
> 
>   transmit works like this:
>   1. Reclaim validated tx used entries.
>   2. Take a free slot; if none, reply busy.
>   3. Write the header (zeros) and the frame into the slot.
>   4. Publish to avail and notify queue 1.
>   5. Reply.
> 
>   It never blocks on anything but its own receive.
> - **Rx thread.** Makes its own map_device and dma_alloc for the RX region, fills its rings and posts all 16 buffers. It then sends the region's physical address to the serving thread, which programs queue 0 and sets DRIVER_OK. Its loop:
>   1. wait_irq, read InterruptStatus and write InterruptACK.
>   2. Drain validated rx entries: copy each frame into a fresh 1-page Buffer, repost the slot.
>   3. send the frame to ipd, with a 50 ms timeout. On Timeout/Busy/Refused it drops the frame and reuses the buffer; drops are counted.
> 
>   It blocks only itself.
> - **Why this does not deadlock.** ipd (one thread) calls netd.transmit, and netd's serving thread always answers promptly. netd's rx thread may block in send to ipd, but that holds up nothing ipd waits for. No transfer is made within one process, so the open question 138 is not touched.
> 
> **Interface to ipd.** This is the IO-ARCHITECTURE "interface capability". Proposed tables: netif goes in IO-ARCHITECTURE's netd note (its own endpoint, opcodes from 1); frame goes in ipd's table (section 3).
> 
> ```
> [wire: netif]
> | Opcode | Message  | Fields         | Reply                  |
> | 1      | info     | -              | mac: u64, mtu: u32     |   (inline, 12 bytes)
> | 2      | transmit | frame: bytes   | -                      |   (buffer; lend 1 page)
> [wire-errors: netif]  2 not_permitted, 3 too_many (frame > 1514 or < 14), 4 busy (tx ring full), 5 failed (device broken)
> ```
> 
> - **Startup handles** (Q149 recommendation, NAME / NAME-irq): `netd` (receive right), `net` (MMIO with DMA), `net-irq`, and `ipd` (a send handle to ipd's endpoint with ipd's ingress badge).
> - **Argument:** `client=<badge>`, the only badge allowed info and transmit. Any other badge or a labelled caller gets not_permitted. A send to netd is dropped and its handles closed.
> - **Exit codes, as blkd:** NO_ENDPOINT, NO_DEVICE, NO_NIC, BAD_ARGS, RECEIVE_FAILED.
> - **netd's note** in IO-ARCHITECTURE Networking gets: what it is trusted for, bounds (16/16 slots, 1514 B, 10 s), each error's meaning, and the Q147 residual.

> ## 2. ipd:lan on smoltcp
> 
> **Dependency (checked here, read-only).**

> - License 0BSD, rust-version 1.91; the local toolchain is rustc 1.98.1.
> - A scratch crate in /tmp with the feature set in decision 1 **builds no_std for both riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf and riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf** (release).
> - Transitive normal dependencies:
> 
>   | Crate | Version | License | Lines |
>   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
>   | managed | 0.8.0 | 0BSD | 1.7k, no unsafe |
>   | heapless | 0.9.3 | MIT/Apache | 20k, about 319 unsafe mentions |
>   | hash32 | 0.3.1 | MIT/Apache | |
>   | stable_deref_trait | 1.2.1 | MIT/Apache | |
>   | byteorder | 1.5 | Unlicense/MIT | |

> 
> - smoltcp itself is deny(unsafe_code) except rand.rs (PCG32) and phy/sys, which we exclude.
> 
> **Tenet 5 treatment.** ipd is a userspace sink, not the kernel TCB, but a compromise reaches every unlabelled user's traffic.
> - Pin with =0.14.0 and Cargo.lock. **Do not vendor**: tenet 5 asks vendoring of privileged code; owner may overrule.
> - We **read** the modules we link: iface/{interface,neighbor,route}, socket/tcp, storage, wire/{ethernet,arp,ipv4,tcp,ip}. The reading notes go in ipd's crate docs.
> - "A dependency that panics on malformed input is a DoS bug in us", so ipd's fuzz target feeds arbitrary frames through Interface::poll.
> - **No other new crates.**
> 
> **Crate `servers/ipd`** (redoubt-ipd; lib + bin ipd; depends on redoubt-rt, redoubt-wire and smoltcp). forbid(unsafe_code): ipd needs none. Files:
> 
> - `src/args.rs`: strict parse of the arguments. Any error means exit BAD_ARGS, failing closed at boot.
>   - `addr=A.B.C.D/len` (exactly one), `gateway=A.B.C.D` (optional).
>   - `self=prefix` (at most 8), `ingress=<badge>` (netd's).
>   - `scope=<badge>:<rule>[,<rule>]` with rule `c:A.B.C.D/len:lo-hi` or `l:port` (at most 8 rules per badge, at most 8 root badges, badges < 2^63).
> - `src/scope.rs`: Rule, Scope, contains, permits_connect, permits_listen, the self set. Pure, with proptests.
> - `src/link.rs`: a smoltcp phy::Device over a Netif trait. On the target that is calls to netd (a reusable 1-page lend and a 100 ms timeout; failure drops the frame). In tests it is an in-memory pipe. rx is a single slot filled from ingress sends.
> - `src/stack.rs`: the Interface plus SocketSet, socket table (id to owner badge, lineage, state, parked waiters), ephemeral ports from `random`, per-socket timeouts.
> - `src/fs.rs`: the FileServer for the /net tree (section 3). `src/server.rs`: the loop glue and typed grant.
> - `src/bin/ipd.rs`: one thread (below). `tests/*.rs`, and `fuzz/` (excluded crate).
> 
> **The ipd loop (one thread; the consoled shape plus smoltcp):**
> 
> ```
> loop:
>   now = time_now()
>   answer expired parked calls (Rerror "timeout")
>   iface.poll(now)                  -> tx via netd.transmit
>   resume parked calls whose socket changed (readable / established / closed / writable)
>   timeout = min(parked.next_deadline, iface.poll_delay)
>   receive(ipd, timeout, max_transfer = 1):
>     labelled caller (call or send)   -> refused before anything else (section 4)
>     send from the ingress badge, op frame
>                                      -> push into the rx slot, poll now; the Buffer drop unmaps
>     other send                       -> drop, close handles, unmap
>     call                             -> serve_parking with own(): grant(16) or not_permitted
>     abandoned                        -> parked.abandoned
>     timeout                          -> continue
> ```
> 
> **Startup handles:** `ipd` (receive right) and `netd` (ipd's badged handle to netd). At start ipd calls netd.info for the MAC and refuses to start without it.
> 
> ## 3. /net over 9P and the IP-prefix-and-port capability
> 
> ### 3.1 The tree (NAMESPACES "The network tree", made concrete)
> 
> ```
> /             the connection's root; its node carries the connection's scope id
> /tcp/         lists only THIS connection's sockets (no leaky state)
> /tcp/clone    read at offset 0 allocates socket N (charged) and returns N (u32)
> /tcp/N/ctl    Twrite: typed ops (3.2); Tread: status (u32 state), PARKS while connecting or listening
> /tcp/N/data   read: bytes, PARKS when empty (0 = peer closed); write: bytes (backpressure: decision 4)
> /tcp/N/remote read: addr: bytes[4], port: u16 (typed)
> ```
> 
> - **Why read-to-allocate instead of Plan 9's open-and-retarget.** The skeleton cannot move a fid's node on open, and a node holds no resource. So clone hands out N by read.
> - **Socket lifetime.** A socket lives until ctl close (graceful, freed after TIME-WAIT), abort, or disconnect of its connection (which aborts all of that connection's sockets). The admission charge bounds a sloppy client to its own bucket, and a launcher's disconnect on child exit reclaims everything (CONTAINMENT: disconnect frees a connection's state).
> - **Visibility.** A walk to another connection's N is "not found". FileServer::labels() is [] for every node.
> 
> ### 3.2 ctl operations
> 
> WIRE: one Twrite per op, the opcode as a u32, then the buffer-shaped fields. The table is proposed for NAMESPACES:
> 
> ```
> [wire: net_ctl]
> | 1 | connect | addr: bytes (4, IPv4, network order), port: u16 | - |
> | 2 | listen  | port: u16                                    | - |
> | 3 | close   | -                                            | - |
> | 4 | abort   | -                                            | - |
> [wire-errors: net_ctl] 2 not_permitted, 3 in_use, 4 too_many, 5 state, 6 unreachable, 7 refused, 8 timeout
> ```
> 
> - **Scope refusals are synchronous.** connect checks the self set, then the scope, then state, **before** smoltcp sees anything. A refusal is an Rerror naming the error. Success means the attempt started. The client then reads ctl, which parks until the socket is established or fails.
> - **Listen.** listen puts N into LISTEN on the interface address. Reading ctl parks until a peer connects, and then N is that connection (smoltcp semantics). For a backlog of K, the holder keeps K listening sockets.
>   - **Only one lineage may hold a port.** A port listened on by one root-badge lineage is in_use for any other, so "ipd:lan delivers port 22 only to sshd" holds even with several listen grants.
>   - Any remote may connect to a listener, since the spec scopes listen by port only.
> 
> ### 3.3 The capability: representation, granting, checking
> 
> - **Representation.** A Scope is at most 8 rules:
>   - Connect{prefix: IPv4 net + len, ports: lo..=hi}
>   - Listen{ports: lo..=hi}
> - **Wire compound** (WIRE's "compound values are a bytes field whose layout is stated"): count: u8, then per rule kind: u8 (1 connect, 2 listen), addr: bytes[4] (network order; 0 for listen), len: u8 (at most 32), lo: u16, hi: u16, with lo <= hi.
> - **Root scopes.** init mints ipd's badges from the manifest; ipd's scope= arguments say what each root badge means.
>   - Milestone-1 manifest: steward badge = c:0.0.0.0/0:1-65535; sshd badge = l:22; netd = the ingress badge, which has no /net.
>   - The manifest's per-principal net scope (INIT.md) is applied by the steward via grant.
> - **Granting.** Typed grant(scope: bytes) -> conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64 (ipd's ninep table, opcode 16). Every requested rule must lie inside one held rule: the same kind, prefix contained, port range contained. Anything wider is not_permitted, so a grant can never widen or add listen.
>   - It is minted through the skeleton's Minted table with the new root node carrying the scope (the mint_rooted addition), so it gets a random badge above 2^63, a random id, answer-168 rollback and admission State.
>   - new_connection("") gives the same scope (launchers); new_connection("tcp") also keeps the scope.
> - **Release.** ninep_common disconnect(id) frees that connection, everything minted under it, and aborts their sockets. Only the id's holder may name it (not_yours).
> - **Checking.** On every connect(addr, port):
>   1. addr in the self set: not_permitted, whatever the scope (decision 6).
>   2. Otherwise at least one Connect rule must contain (addr, port).
> 
>   On listen(p): a Listen rule must contain p, and the lineage rule holds (3.2).
> 
> ```
> [wire: ipd ninep]
> | Opcode | Kind | Message | Fields        | Reply                               |
> | 16     | call | grant   | scope: bytes  | conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64   |
> | 17     | send | frame   | frame: bytes  | -                                   |   (ingress badge only; 1-page transfer)
> [wire-errors: ipd] 2 not_permitted, 3 too_many
> ```
> 
> ### 3.4 The self set
> 
> **Never includes the box's own addresses, loopback included.** It holds:
> - addr's host address, the network and directed-broadcast addresses of addr/len, and 255.255.255.255;
> - 127.0.0.0/8 and 0.0.0.0/8;
> - 224.0.0.0/4 and 240.0.0.0/4 (not unicast);
> - every self= argument. On QEMU the manifest names 10.0.2.2/32: slirp maps the gateway to host loopback, where hostfwd leads back to the guest's port 22. That is the CAPABILITIES "loopback login" route.
> 
> The check runs **before** the scope check, so a manifest that wrongly scoped 0.0.0.0/0 still cannot reach the box. The check sits in scope.rs and is one function, covered by a table test.
> 
> ## 4. Confinement
> 
> - **One ipd per network or trust domain.** ipd keeps no statics and no cross-instance state. Its whole configuration is its arguments and handles, so two instances are two processes with two budgets. netd pushes to exactly one ipd, so a second trust domain on one NIC needs a second NIC/netd pair or linkd (Later).
> - **The manifest side is R3's.** init refuses a confined manifest in which differing label sets share an ipd:* / netd. That is WP-R3's refusal, not D3's.
> - **A labelled domain gets no /net.** The steward and manifest give it none (S2/R3). **ipd refuses labelled callers regardless.**
>   - The check runs at the top of the loop, before 9P, ninep_common, grant or admission, on every call and send, keyed by kernel-attached caller.labels, which cannot be forged.
>   - So a labelled budget that obtained an ipd handle anyway gets not_permitted / Rerror on everything and never opens a bucket (CONTAINMENT: sinks are cleared for nothing).
> - **netd** accepts only its configured client badge and unlabelled callers.
> 
> ## 5. Resource accounting and DoS
> 
> **ipd admission** (libs/rt Admission, per (account, label set); account 0 per badge):
> - Limits: buckets 8, in_flight 5 (8 x 5 = 40, which is at most MAX_OPEN_CALLS - OPEN_CALL_HEADROOM = 48), files 24 (fids), state 16 (minted connections plus sockets, charged as Resource::State through admission_mut()).
> - sshd's bucket (a system caller, per badge) needs about 4 listening sockets plus one per session, which fits in 16.
> - Every bucket at its cap must fit ipd's budget (Limits::fits):
>   - Socket buffers are 8 KiB rx + 8 KiB tx, so 8 x 16 x 16 KiB = 2 MiB.
>   - Parked lends are up to 16 pages each: 40 x 68 KiB, about 2.7 MiB.
>   - Plus about 1 MiB of heap and smoltcp.
>   - Proposed ipd budget: 8 MiB.
> 
> **Parked calls:**
> - A ctl read waiting to connect or accept has a **60 s** server deadline. A data read has **30 s** and then answers Rerror "timeout"; the client re-reads. It waits on the network, not a person, so it is not the console's FOREVER exception.
> - Abandoned calls are answered at once.
> - The serve before resuming comes from Parked.
> 
> **What a hostile caller can exhaust:** only its own bucket (and its share inside it), plus the stated shared cap of 8 bucket slots.
> - Handles a request brings are closed.
> - Client sends are dropped and their transfer unmapped; max_transfer = 1, and larger transfers are Refused by the kernel.
> - The work of one request is bounded to at most one msize copy and one socket operation.
> - **The pinned-open-calls attack.** Bob parks 64 calls and gets 5 parked, the rest refused. Even at MAX_OPEN_CALLS, R4a still delivers sends, so netd's frames and abandonment notices keep arriving.
> 
> **What a hostile network peer can exhaust:**
> - A listener's sockets. A SYN flood holds them in SYN-RECEIVED until a 10 s timeout, which is the stated residual; the backlog is K sockets.
> - A connection's own 8 KiB buffers.
> - smoltcp's fixed neighbor cache, route table and reassembly assembler, which are sized at compile time. IP fragments are dropped, since reassembly is off.
> - ipd CPU per frame, at ipd's ordinary weight.
> - netd CPU at weight 1000 (stated residual).
> - One page per frame in transit. If ipd's budget is short, the kernel says Refused and the frame is dropped.
> 
> There is no unbounded queue anywhere:
> - The device holds at most 16 rx buffers.
> - netd has one send in flight.
> - ipd has a one-frame rx slot, consumed by poll straight away.
> - netd's tx ring answers busy, and smoltcp retransmits.
> 
> **netd:** one client badge; transmit is bounded (1514 B) and never parks; 16 + 16 slots.

Event: `f3989b652076c8648115f0b1a2434dec` · 2026-09-24T20:21:24Z

> The rulings are recorded in the plan file (a "Rulings received" section at the top). Write::Wait will be **general** in libs/rt: any FileServer may return it, and in M1 only /net data does. The NAMESPACES amendment will say exactly that. v2 will fold in the red team's findings when they arrive. Still PLAN ONLY.
> 
> **Decision 11: mitigation, no fork.**
> 
> **What smoltcp 0.14 offers.** No direct hook. Its Rand is pub(crate), and the seed exists only as Config::random_seed at Interface::new. The ISN comes from cx.rand() in two places: tcp::Socket::connect(cx, ..) for active opens (tcp.rs:1063), and SYN processing in ingress for passive opens (tcp.rs:1919).
> 
> **The public API is enough.** Sockets live in the SocketSet, apart from the Interface. And connect takes any &mut Context (Interface::context() is public).
> 
> So:
> 1. **Active open.** ipd builds a throwaway Interface with random_seed = the kernel CSPRNG's random_u64(). It has the same hardware address, IP address and default route, and uses a null device. ipd calls socket.connect(fresh.context(), ..) on it, with the local port also from `random`.
> 2. **Passive open.** ipd parses its one-frame rx slot with smoltcp::wire. If the frame is IPv4 TCP with SYN and no ACK addressed to ipd, it is processed with fresh.poll_ingress_single(now, link, sockets) on a freshly seeded throwaway. The SYN-ACK leaves later through the main interface's egress. Every other frame goes through the main interface.
> 
> So the main interface's PRNG never produces an ISN. One helper builds both interfaces from the same arguments, so their configurations cannot drift.
> 
> **What each ISN is.** PCG32 output #2 of an independent 64-bit CSPRNG seed.
> - Output #1 seeds ipv4_id, which is never emitted: with fragmentation off, wire/ipv4.rs:604 always emits ident 0.
> - TCP timestamps stay off (tsval_generator None).
> - Cost: one `random` syscall and one small Interface::new per connect or SYN. That is bounded per frame, SYN flood included.
> 
> **Tests.** An injected seed source checks that:
> - each connect or accepted SYN consumes exactly one seed;
> - the ISN of connection k equals output 2 of seed k;
> - none of 1000 ISNs appears among the first 10k outputs of the main interface's seed (a mutation guard).
> 
> **Residual, stated precisely.**
> - **Blind off-path injection.** The attacker must guess an in-window sequence number: with an 8 KiB window, about 2^19 tries per connection, the same as any random-ISN stack. The worst case is a reset, or injected bytes that SSH's transport MAC rejects, which ends the session. That is a denial of service, not a compromise.
> - **Cross-user connection-rate channel.** The shared observable PRNG is gone. Ports come from `random`, and no IP-ID counter is emitted. What remains between **unlabelled** users sharing one ipd are admission-slot occupancy and CPU/queue timing, which CONTAINMENT already states. No label boundary is involved, since labelled callers are refused.

>   - it covers blkd too.
> - Stack overflow and other non-panic faults remain the residual.
> 
> **R2: the pcap check** (section 6.4). It asserts:
> - no guest-originated SYN without ACK to self_forbidden;
> - no non-TCP IPv4;
> - ARP only for the gateway;
> - guest-originated means an Ethernet source other than 52:55:0a:00:02:02.
> 
> It fails closed on a missing, empty, truncated or malformed capture. It requires the control SYN to 10.0.9.100:7 to be present. self_forbidden is one constant in tests/net, and a host test checks it against the rig's self= arguments.
> 
> **R3: bucket exhaustion.** The rig's ipd has buckets=4, and the rig's own account-0 granting badge counts as one. 3 unlabelled accounts must succeed and a 4th must get too_many.
> 
> **R4: admission overrides.**
> - Overrides apply only when account == 0, on the exact root badge. sshd and the steward call ipd on their root badges.
> - Badges at or above 2^63 and duplicate badges are refused.
> - ipd refuses to start unless sum(overrides) + (buckets - #overrides) x default <= 48, and fits holds.
> - Milestone arithmetic: sshd 24 + steward 2 (its own bucket) + 4 x 5 = 46 <= 48.
> 
> **Closed-with-notes items, all taken:**
> - the helper's file name gets a random suffix with an O_EXCL retry, and the helper refuses to echo if it can't record;
> - a qemu.rs unit test that every [net] case has restrict=on;
> - a thread_create failure reclaims the Box, resets the device and doesn't retry; unsafe-budget entry;
> - the panic hook is set-once, runs before report_panic, has its own once-flag, is bounded and doesn't allocate, and its unsafe is counted in rt's budget;
> - no ISN fallback if random fails, and connect uses an explicit local address;
> - receive(0) is needed only after a park;
> - no-link mode is entered only on an info failure, a non-unicast MAC or transmit `failed`, with info retried with backoff and every check kept;
> - martian-source drop (own address, 127/8, 0/8; not 10.0.2.2);
> - attackers and labelled programs get no console, and verdict lines are anchored to [net-rig].
> 
> **R5: OWNER DECISIONS 1-13** cover:
> - smoltcp pinned and not vendored (owner flag);
> - IPv4, TCP and static configuration, with UDP deferred;
> - the WIRE kind column;
> - libs/rt: Write::Wait (general), mint_rooted, set_panic_hook and the Admission override;

> Defensive change for netd, from K5 review 5: on QEMU virt, an interrupt raised while the IRQ object is masked (between receives) was lost once, on a driver's FIRST receive. No kernel defect was found, and it's being followed up with K3. Make netd robust to a missed interrupt: after every IRQ receive returns (and once right after DRIVER_OK, before the first receive), drain the used rings until empty, and re-check the used ring index before blocking again, so a lost first edge can't stall rx or tx. Add a host test where the fake device completes a buffer without raising the interrupt, before the first receive, and netd still delivers it. Include it in checkpoint (c).
